questions.question: In 2025, which company has partnered with the Archaeological Survey of India (ASI) to restore heritage water bodies?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Bisleri**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Bisleri**, a leading packaged drinking water company in India, has partnered with the **Archaeological Survey of India (ASI)** in 2025 to restore heritage water bodies across the country.
 
• The initiative is aimed at **reviving traditional water conservation systems** that were historically significant and played a key role in maintaining water availability.
 
• This partnership focuses on **restoration and rejuvenation of ancient stepwells, ponds, and other water bodies** situated at heritage sites under the protection of ASI.
 
• The collaboration aligns with the Indian government’s emphasis on **cultural preservation** and sustainable water resource management.
 
• Under this initiative, Bisleri has pledged to use its expertise and resources to ensure the **scientific and eco-friendly restoration** of these water bodies, while also raising awareness about their historical and environmental significance.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Archaeological Survey of India (ASI):**

 
 
• The ASI, under the Ministry of Culture, is responsible for the **protection and preservation of India’s cultural heritage**, including monuments, archaeological sites, and remains of national importance.
 
• It was established in **1861** by Alexander Cunningham and has since played a vital role in safeguarding India’s rich historical legacy.
 
• As of now, ASI protects and maintains over **3,600 monuments**, including ancient water structures.
 
 
 
• **Heritage Water Bodies:**
 
 
• These include traditional water storage systems such as **stepwells, kunds, baolis, and lakes**, which were constructed to meet water needs in historic times.
 
• Many of these structures, apart from serving as water sources, were architectural marvels and had **religious and cultural significance**.
 
• The restoration of these water bodies is crucial for addressing **water scarcity** issues and promoting heritage tourism.
 
 
 
• **About Bisleri:**
 
 
• Founded in **1969**, Bisleri is one of India’s most recognized brands in the **packaged drinking water industry**.
 
• The company is known for its focus on sustainability and has initiated various **CSR activities** related to water conservation.
 
• Its **‘Bottles for Change’ campaign** is a notable initiative aimed at recycling plastic waste and promoting environmental awareness.
 
 
 
• **Government Initiatives for Water Conservation:**
 
 
• Programs like **Jal Shakti Abhiyan** and **Atal Bhujal Yojana** have been launched to address water conservation and management issues in India.
 
• These programs focus on **rainwater harvesting**, rejuvenation of traditional water bodies, and groundwater recharge.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• Restoration of heritage water bodies helps in **combating water scarcity** and promotes environmental sustainability.
 
• It also contributes to **heritage tourism**, creating awareness about India’s rich cultural and architectural legacy.
 
• Partnerships between private entities like Bisleri and public institutions like ASI exemplify the importance of **public-private collaboration** in addressing pressing environmental and heritage conservation challenges.
 
• The initiative aligns with global efforts toward achieving the **Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs)**, particularly SDG 6 (Clean Water and Sanitation) and SDG 11 (Sustainable Cities and Communities).

questions.question: Indian railways is working with which organisation to make trains safer?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**ISRO**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Indian Railways is collaborating with the **Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO)** to enhance safety measures in train operations by leveraging advanced satellite technology.
 
• ISRO provides satellite-based real-time tracking systems, which are used to monitor train movements and prevent accidents by identifying potential hazards.
 
• The **GAGAN (GPS Aided GEO Augmented Navigation)** system, developed jointly by ISRO and the Airports Authority of India (AAI), is being utilized to improve the accuracy of train location data.
 
• This collaboration focuses on developing an automated system to avoid accidents caused by unmanned level crossings and to ensure better signaling systems across the railway network.
 
• The use of satellite technology aids in timely disaster response and effective resource allocation during emergencies, thereby enhancing the safety and efficiency of Indian Railways.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **DRDO (Defence Research and Development Organisation):**

 
 
• DRDO is primarily responsible for developing defense technologies for India's armed forces.
 
• It focuses on areas such as missiles, combat vehicles, radar systems, and advanced electronics, and is not directly involved in railway safety enhancements.
 
 
 
• **NALSAR (National Academy of Legal Studies and Research):**
 
 
• NALSAR is a premier law university in India, known for its legal education and research programs.
 
• While it contributes to legal and policy frameworks, it is not involved in technological advancements for railway safety.
 
 
 
• **ICAR (Indian Council of Agricultural Research):**
 
 
• ICAR is an autonomous body responsible for promoting agricultural education, research, and extension in India.
 
• Its focus is on advancements in agriculture and related fields, making it unrelated to railway safety measures.

questions.question: The headquarters of WADA are in ______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Montréal**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **World Anti-Doping Agency (WADA)** is an independent international organization that promotes, coordinates, and monitors the fight against doping in sports worldwide.
 
• The **headquarters of WADA** is located in **Montréal, Canada**. It serves as the central hub for the agency's global operations and initiatives.
 
• WADA was established in **1999** after the World Conference on Doping in Sport and is jointly funded by the **International Olympic Committee (IOC)** and national governments.
 
• Montréal was chosen as the headquarters due to its strategic location, accessibility, and status as a hub for international organizations.
 
• Its primary mission includes developing and implementing anti-doping policies, conducting research, and promoting awareness to ensure fair play in sports.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **About WADA:**

 
 
• The agency’s foundation was laid during the **World Conference on Doping in Sport**, held in Lausanne, Switzerland, in **1999**.
 
• WADA’s core functions include **Code compliance monitoring**, **scientific research**, **education**, and **anti-doping program development.**
 
• The organization operates on the basis of the **World Anti-Doping Code**, which is a universal document ensuring consistency in anti-doping rules and regulations globally.
 
• WADA also accredits **anti-doping laboratories** worldwide to ensure high standards of testing.
 
 
 
• **Why Montréal?**
 
 
• Montréal is a prominent city in Canada known for its cosmopolitan environment, making it ideal for hosting international organizations.
 
• The city provides excellent infrastructure and accessibility for global operations and communication.
 
• Montréal is also home to several other major international organizations, such as the **International Civil Aviation Organization (ICAO).**
 
 
 
• **Other Locations Considered:**
 
 
• **Paris:** Known for hosting various international agencies, but it was not selected as WADA's headquarters.
 
• **Geneva:** A hub for many global organizations like the World Health Organization (WHO), but not chosen for WADA.
 
• **Vienna:** Hosts organizations like the International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA), but it did not meet the criteria for WADA’s operations.
 
 
 
• **WADA’s Achievements:**
 
 
• Development of the **Athlete Biological Passport** to monitor biological markers of doping.
 
• Implementation of the **Prohibited List**, updated annually, to identify banned substances and methods.
 
• Global initiatives like **Play True Day** to raise awareness about anti-doping.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **WADA’s Governance:**

 
 
• The agency is governed by a foundation board comprising representatives from the **sport movement** and **national governments.**
 
• The **Executive Committee**, composed of 12 members, is responsible for making decisions on behalf of the foundation board.
 
 
 
• **Global Anti-Doping Efforts:**
 
 
• WADA collaborates with national anti-doping organizations (NADOs) and regional anti-doping organizations (RADOs).
 
• Its efforts ensure a unified approach to combating doping in sports across all countries.

questions.question: In July 2025, which investigative authority unearthed over ₹24 crore in unaccounted assets in Karnataka?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Karnataka Lokayukta**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Karnataka Lokayukta** is an independent anti-corruption ombudsman and investigative authority in the state of Karnataka, India.
 
• In **July 2025**, the Karnataka Lokayukta uncovered **over ₹24 crore** in unaccounted assets in a high-profile corruption case in Karnataka.
 
• The Lokayukta conducted **search and seizure operations** at various locations associated with government officials and private entities, leading to the revelation of these unaccounted assets.
 
• The investigation involved tracking financial irregularities, disproportionate assets, and suspected misuse of public office, which are core areas of Lokayukta’s jurisdiction.
 
• This operation underscores the **role of the Karnataka Lokayukta** in combating corruption and ensuring accountability in public administration.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Karnataka Lokayukta:**

 
 
• Established under the Karnataka Lokayukta Act, 1984, it is one of the pioneering anti-corruption bodies in India.
 
• It is empowered to investigate allegations of corruption, misuse of power, and maladministration against public servants, including elected representatives, government officials, and private entities involved in public dealings.
 
• The Lokayukta operates independently of the state government, ensuring an unbiased investigation process.
 
• The Lokayukta’s findings and recommendations hold significant weight, often leading to disciplinary or legal action.
 
 
 
• **Other Investigative Authorities:**
 
 
• **Income Tax Department:** This authority investigates tax evasion, monitors financial transactions, and ensures compliance with income tax laws. However, it primarily focuses on tax-related offenses, not broader corruption cases.
 
• **Enforcement Directorate (ED):** The ED enforces laws related to money laundering and foreign exchange violations under FEMA and PMLA. It investigates financial crimes but does not directly deal with public administration corruption.
 
• **Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI):** The CBI investigates cases of corruption, economic offenses, and special crimes across India. However, state-level investigations like this one often fall under the jurisdiction of Lokayuktas or state-specific bodies.
 
 
 
• **Disproportionate Assets Cases:**
 
 
• These cases involve public officials possessing wealth that significantly exceeds their known sources of income.
 
• Such investigations require collaboration between multiple agencies, including Lokayuktas, tax departments, and forensic auditors.
 
• Unaccounted assets often include cash, gold, property, and other investments.
 
 
 
• **Anti-Corruption Efforts in India:**
 
 
• India has multiple anti-corruption bodies, including the **Central Vigilance Commission (CVC)**, Lokayuktas, and the CBI, to combat corruption at various levels.
 
• The **Prevention of Corruption Act, 1988**, is the primary legislation dealing with corruption in public offices.
 
• Recent amendments and stricter enforcement mechanisms aim to improve transparency and accountability in governance.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Key Characteristics of Lokayuktas:**

 
 
• Lokayuktas are state-level anti-corruption bodies that complement the role of the Central Vigilance Commission at the national level.
 
• They investigate complaints from the public regarding corruption, abuse of power, or maladministration in state government offices.
 
• Lokayuktas have the authority to investigate even high-ranking officials, including the Chief Minister, in some states.
 
 
 
• **Significant Cases Handled by Lokayuktas:**
 
 
• In Karnataka, the Lokayukta has previously investigated several high-profile cases, including illegal mining scandals and disproportionate assets cases involving prominent politicians.
 
• Its proactive role has set benchmarks for anti-corruption efforts in other states.

questions.question: As of July 2025, Bharat Electronics Limited has been awarded with which of the following CPSE status?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Navratna**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Bharat Electronics Limited (BEL)** is a state-owned aerospace and defence company that holds the prestigious **Navratna** status among Central Public Sector Enterprises (CPSEs).
 
• The **Navratna** status was conferred upon **BEL** by the Government of India in **June 2007**, providing it with enhanced financial and operational autonomy to compete in the global market.
 
• Established in **1954** in **Bengaluru, Karnataka**, the company functions under the administrative control of the **Ministry of Defence**.
 
• **BEL** was set up in collaboration with **CSF, France** (now part of the **Thales Group**), primarily to manufacture basic communication equipment for the Indian Armed Forces.
 
• The company operates **nine manufacturing units** across India, located in cities including **Ghaziabad, Pune, Hyderabad, Chennai, Machilipatnam, Panchkula, Kotdwara, and Navi Mumbai**.
 
• As of **July 2025**, **BEL** remains a key **Navratna** entity, specializing in **Radars, Missile Systems, Electronic Warfare, Sonars**, and even civilian products like **Electronic Voting Machines (EVMs)** and **VVPATs**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Classification of CPSEs**: The Department of Public Enterprises (**DPE**), under the **Ministry of Finance**, classifies **Central Public Sector Enterprises** into three categories: **Maharatna, Navratna, and Miniratna** (Category I and II).
 
• **Navratna Criteria**: To be eligible for **Navratna** status, a **CPSE** must be a **Miniratna Category-I** and a **Schedule ‘A’** company, have obtained an **‘Excellent’** or **‘Very Good’** rating in the **Memorandum of Understanding (MoU)** system in three of the last five years, and have a composite score of **60 or above** in six performance parameters.
 
• **Maharatna Category**: This is the highest status, introduced in **May 2010**. Companies like **BHEL, ONGC, and NTPC** hold this status. To be a **Maharatna**, a company must have a **Navratna** status, be listed on the **Indian stock exchange**, and have an average annual **net profit** of over **Rs. 5,000 crore** during the last **3 years**.
 
• **Miniratna Category-I**: These companies must have made a profit in the last **three years** continuously, pre-tax profit of **Rs. 30 crore** or more in at least one of the three years, and have a **positive net worth**.
 
• **Miniratna Category-II**: These companies must have made a profit for the last **three years** continuously and should have a **positive net worth** to be eligible for autonomy.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Financial Autonomy**: A **Navratna** company like **BEL** has the power to invest up to **Rs. 1,000 crore** or **15% of its net worth** on a single project without seeking prior approval from the Central Government.
 
• **Global Reach**: **Navratna** status allows these firms to establish **Joint Ventures** and **Subsidiaries** in India or abroad, facilitating global expansion and technology acquisition.
 
• **Diversification**: While **BEL** is primarily a defence electronics firm, it has diversified into **Solar Power, Homeland Security, Smart Cities, and Medical Electronics** (notably manufacturing ventilators during the **2020 pandemic**).
 
• **MoU Parameters**: The six parameters for **Navratna** scoring include **Net Profit to Net Worth**, **Manpower Cost to total Cost of Production**, **Profit Before Depreciation, Interest and Taxes (PBDIT) to Capital Employed**, and **Earnings Per Share (EPS)**, among others.

questions.question: Which body was established in 1986 in India to manage national waterways?

options.text: Ministry of River Navigation of India
National Water Transport Board of India

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Inland Waterways Authority of India**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Inland Waterways Authority of India (IWAI)** was established on **27 October 1986** under the **Inland Waterways Authority of India Act, 1985**.
 
• It functions under the **Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways** and is responsible for the regulation and development of **inland waterways** for shipping and navigation.
 
• The IWAI is tasked with developing and maintaining **National Waterways (NW)**. As of now, there are **111 National Waterways** in India, with five of them being operational for cargo and passenger movement.
 
• Some of the key National Waterways under IWAI include **NW-1 (Ganga River), NW-2 (Brahmaputra River), and NW-3 (Kerala Backwaters)**.
 
• It also aims to promote **eco-friendly and cost-effective transportation** of goods and passengers, reducing dependence on road and rail transport.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **National Waterways in India:**

 
 
• India has declared **111 rivers or river stretches** as National Waterways under the **National Waterways Act, 2016**.
 
• The **five key operational waterways** include:
 
 
• **NW-1:** Allahabad-Haldia stretch of Ganga-Bhagirathi-Hooghly River system (1620 km).
 
• **NW-2:** Sadiya-Dhubri stretch of Brahmaputra River (891 km).
 
• **NW-3:** West Coast Canal from Kottapuram to Kollam along with Champakara and Udyogmandal Canals (205 km).
 
• **NW-4:** Kakinada-Pondicherry stretch of canals and Krishna-Godavari rivers (1078 km).
 
• **NW-5:** East Coast Canal integrated with Brahmani and Mahanadi River system (588 km).
 
 
 
 
 
• **Functions of IWAI:**
 
 
• Developing infrastructure for **navigation, including terminals, fairways, and navigation aids**.
 
• Carrying out **hydrographic surveys** and ensuring the provision of navigational safety equipment.
 
• Conducting **economic feasibility studies** for inland water transport projects.
 
• Promoting **public-private partnerships (PPP)** in developing inland waterways projects.
 
 
 
• **Importance of Inland Water Transport (IWT):**
 
 
• IWT is a **cost-effective and environmentally friendly** mode of transport.
 
• It is particularly suitable for transporting **bulk goods** such as coal, cement, food grains, and fertilizers.
 
• The development of IWT reduces the burden on **roads and railways**, lowering transportation costs and pollution.
 
 
 
• **Challenges in IWT Development:**
 
 
• Lack of **adequate infrastructure** such as terminals, jetties, and dredging facilities.
 
• Seasonal variations in water levels, especially in rivers like the Ganga and Brahmaputra.
 
• Limited **private sector participation** and funding for inland waterway projects.
 
• Need for improved coordination among **state governments** and central authorities for efficient operation.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Other Authorities in Water Management:**

 
 
• **Ministry of Jal Shakti:** Responsible for overall water resource management in India.
 
• **Central Water Commission (CWC):** Engaged in managing and developing India's water resources.
 
• **National Water Development Agency (NWDA):** Focuses on interlinking rivers and water resource planning.
 
 
 
• **Global Examples of Inland Waterways:**
 
 
• **Mississippi River (USA):** One of the busiest inland waterways in the world.
 
• **Rhine River (Europe):** A vital trade route for Germany and surrounding countries.
 
• **Yangtze River (China):** Used for bulk goods transport and passenger services.

questions.question: ​The 'Anusandhan National Research Foundation (ANRF) Act, 2023' was passed to create a new body for ?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Funding scientific research**__.

**__Key Points__**

__

• The **Anusandhan National Research Foundation (ANRF) Act, 2023** was enacted to establish a premier national body that provides high-level strategic direction for **scientific research** in India.

• The primary objective of the **ANRF** is to seed, grow, and promote **Research and Development (R&D)** and foster a culture of research and innovation throughout India’s universities, colleges, and research institutions.

• The body is designed to bridge the gap between **academia**, **industry**, and **government departments**, ensuring that scientific advancements are translated into tangible technological and social benefits.

• The Act aligns with the recommendations of the **National Education Policy (NEP) 2020**, aiming to significantly increase the gross expenditure on **R&D** by encouraging **private sector** participation and investment.

 **Additional Information__**

• **Repeal of SERB**:

• The **ANRF** replaces the **Science and Engineering Research Board (SERB)**, which was established by an Act of Parliament in **2008**.

• While **SERB** primarily focused on individual research grants, **ANRF** has a much broader mandate covering **natural sciences**, **mathematics**, **engineering**, **environmental science**, and **social sciences**.

• **Governance Structure**:

• The **Prime Minister of India** is the ex-officio **President** of the Governing Board of the **ANRF**.

• The **Union Minister of Science and Technology** and the **Union Minister of Education** serve as the ex-officio **Vice-Presidents**.

• The **Department of Science and Technology (DST)** acts as the administrative department for the foundation.

• **Financial Framework**:

• The foundation receives funds from the **Consolidated Fund of India**, as well as contributions from **Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR)** funds and other philanthropic sources.

questions.question: Which organisation has been designated as the nodal implementing agency for the Textile Export Facilitation Center (TEFC) scheme?

options.text: Textiles Committee under the Ministry of Textiles

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Textiles Committee under the Ministry of Textiles.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/7a63139f3b57ffe3814d27f8dcaee8cb420142f7146b480d479d526074519671.png] **__In News__**

__
 
• **The Ministry of Textiles announced the establishment of Textile Export Facilitation Centers (TEFC) to strengthen India’s textile exports in global markets.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **Key Points__**

__
 
• **The Textiles Committee under the Ministry of Textiles is the nodal implementing agency for the TEFC scheme.**
 
• Jaipur is one of the six pilot centres selected for the Textile Export Facilitation Center initiative.
 
• The Jaipur centre will promote exports of Rajasthan’s handloom and handicraft products.
 
• The centres will provide services such as FTA/PTA guidance, HS classification support, technical assistance, training programmes and digital helpdesk facilities.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Six Pilot TEFC Centres**__

 __
 
• The pilot centres are located in Karur, Surat, Ichalkaranji, Jaipur, Varanasi and Ludhiana.
 
• These centres were selected based on their importance in textile and handicraft production.
 
 
 
• **FTA/PTA Guidance**__
 __
 
• FTA refers to Free Trade Agreement and PTA refers to Preferential Trade Agreement.
 
• The centres will help exporters understand trade benefits and international market access.
 
 
 
• **HS Classification**__
 __
 
• HS Classification refers to the Harmonized System used for international trade classification of products.
 
• It helps in customs procedures and export documentation.
 
 
 
• **Importance of Jaipur Centre**__
 
 
• The Jaipur centre will support artisans and exporters in accessing global textile markets.
 
• It will strengthen exports of Rajasthan’s traditional handloom and handicraft industries.

questions.question: Which of the following, set up in June 1986, is responsible for the management of civil aerodromes and civil enclaves as well as for maintenance and operation of aeronautical communication systems at all the airports?

• The **National Airports Authority (NAA)** was established in June 1986 under the National Airports Authority Act, 1985.
 
• The NAA was responsible for the management of **civil aerodromes and civil enclaves** across India.
 
• It was also tasked with the maintenance and operation of **aeronautical communication systems** at all airports in the country.
 
• Later, the National Airports Authority merged with the International Airports Authority of India in 1995 to form the **Airports Authority of India (AAI)**.
 
• This merger aimed to improve efficiency in airport management and streamline operations across all civil aviation facilities in India.

• It is a Public-Private Partnership (PPP) between the Airports Authority of India, GMR Group, and other stakeholders.
 
• DIAL focuses on modernization and efficient management of Delhi Airport but is not responsible for other civil aerodromes in India.
 
 
 
• **Airports Authority of India (AAI)**:
 
 
• AAI was formed in 1995 after the merger of the National Airports Authority (NAA) and the International Airports Authority of India (IAAI).
 
• It is responsible for managing and operating airports, providing air navigation services, and ensuring the development and modernization of civil aviation infrastructure in India.
 
• AAI oversees more than 100 airports in India, including both domestic and international airports.
 
 
 
• **Airports Council International (ACI)**:

• It provides a platform for airport operators to exchange best practices, promote airport excellence, and advocate for policies benefiting the aviation industry.
 
• However, ACI is not directly involved in managing or operating airports.

questions.question: Which Indian institution was declared a 'Deemed to be University' in April 2025?

• Located in **Pune**, **Maharashtra**, **FTII** is an autonomous institution functioning under the aegis of the **Ministry of Information and Broadcasting** of the **Government of India**.

questions.question: Which Indian agency is responsible for cyclone warning and tracking?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Indian Meteorological Department (IMD)**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Indian Meteorological Department (IMD)** is the primary agency responsible for **cyclone warnings and tracking** in India.
 
• IMD operates under the **Ministry of Earth Sciences** and was established in **1875** to provide weather-related information and forecasts.
 
• The agency uses advanced technologies such as **satellites, radar systems, and numerical weather prediction models** to track cyclones and issue warnings.
 
• IMD issues cyclone warnings for different regions, categorizing the stages of cyclones into **pre-cyclone watch, cyclone alert, and cyclone warning.**
 
• IMD’s **Regional Specialized Meteorological Centre (RSMC)** based in New Delhi serves as the hub for cyclone monitoring and forecasting in the **North Indian Ocean region**, including the Bay of Bengal and the Arabian Sea.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Central Water Commission (CWC):**

 
 
• The CWC primarily deals with **water resource management**, including flood forecasting and irrigation projects.
 
• It is not directly responsible for **cyclone warnings** but plays a vital role in managing the aftermath, such as flood control.
 
 
 
• **National Remote Sensing Centre (NRSC):**
 
 
• NRSC is a part of **ISRO** and specializes in **satellite-based remote sensing**.
 
• It provides valuable geospatial data that can assist agencies like IMD in cyclone tracking but is not the primary agency for issuing warnings.
 
 
 
• **National Disaster Management Authority (NDMA):**
 
 
• NDMA is India’s apex body responsible for **disaster management**, including preparedness, response, and recovery.
 
• It works in coordination with IMD for disseminating cyclone warnings and managing disaster relief operations.
 
 
 
• **Indian Meteorological Department (IMD):**
 
 
• IMD provides weather forecasts and warnings for **cyclones, heavy rainfall, and other meteorological events**.
 
• Its **Regional Meteorological Centres** and state-specific warning systems ensure localized and effective communication of cyclone risks.
 
• IMD’s warnings are essential for disaster preparedness, helping agencies like NDMA and local governments take timely action.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **IMD's Cyclone Warning System:**

 
 
• IMD’s cyclone warnings consist of **color-coded alerts** such as yellow, orange, and red, indicating the severity of the cyclone.
 
• The warnings are disseminated through **television, radio, social media, and mobile applications** to ensure maximum reach.
 
 
 
• **Use of Satellite Data:**
 
 
• IMD uses data from satellites like **INSAT and METSAT** to monitor cyclone formation and movement.
 
• The integration of satellite data ensures accurate forecasting and timely warnings.
 
 
 
• **Regional Collaboration:**
 
 
• IMD collaborates with regional meteorological centers and international agencies like the **World Meteorological Organization (WMO)** for cyclone monitoring.
 
• This collaboration enhances forecasting accuracy for cyclones affecting neighboring countries.

questions.question: Who chaired the 10th Governing Council Meeting of the NITI Aayog on 24 May 2025?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Narendra Modi**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Governing Council** of **NITI Aayog** (National Institution for Transforming India) is chaired by the **Prime Minister of India**, who serves as its **Ex-officio Chairperson**. As of the year **2025**, **Shri Narendra Modi** holds this position and thus chaired the **10th Governing Council Meeting** on **24 May 2025**. ***Hence, statement C is correct.***
 
• The meeting focuses on the **National Development Agenda**, involving a shared vision between the **Center and the States** to foster **Cooperative Federalism**.
 
• The **Governing Council** comprises the **Prime Minister**, **Chief Ministers** of all States and Union Territories with Legislatures, and **Lieutenant Governors** of other Union Territories.
 
• Key agendas for the **10th meeting** typically revolve around the roadmap for **Viksit Bharat @ 2047**, emphasizing **economic growth**, **social welfare**, and **infrastructure development**.
 
• **Amit Shah**, **Manohar Lal Khattar**, and **JP Nadda** are high-ranking **Union Ministers** who serve as **Ex-officio members** or **Special Invitees** but do not hold the authority to chair the Governing Council meeting when the Prime Minister is present. ***Hence, statements A, B, and D are incorrect.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **NITI Aayog Establishment:** It was established on **January 1, 2015**, by a resolution of the Union Cabinet. It replaced the **Planning Commission**, which had been in existence since **1950**. Unlike the Planning Commission, which followed a top-down approach, **NITI Aayog** follows a **bottom-up approach**.
 
• **Organizational Structure:** The hierarchy includes a **Vice-Chairperson** (appointed by the PM), a **Chief Executive Officer (CEO)**, **Full-time Members**, **Ex-officio Members** (maximum 4 from the Union Council of Ministers), and **Special Invitees**.
 
• **Hubs of NITI Aayog:** It operates through two main hubs: the **Team India Hub** (carrying the interface of States with the Center) and the **Knowledge and Innovation Hub** (building the think-tank capacity).
 
• **Reports and Indices:** **NITI Aayog** is responsible for publishing several important indices, such as the **SDG India Index**, **Composite Water Management Index**, **School Education Quality Index**, and the **India Innovation Index**.
 
• **Cooperative Federalism:** One of the primary mandates is to recognize that **strong States make a strong Nation**. It provides a platform to resolve inter-sectoral and inter-departmental issues to accelerate the **development agenda**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Role of the Prime Minister:** As the **Chairperson**, the **PM** sets the tone for national priorities. The **Governing Council** meetings are the highest decision-making platform in the organization.
 
• **Membership Nuances:** **Amit Shah** serves as the **Union Minister of Home Affairs**, while **JP Nadda** serves as the **Union Minister of Health and Family Welfare**. Both are **Ex-officio members** of **NITI Aayog** as of **2024-2025**.
 
• **Administrative Location:** The headquarters of **NITI Aayog** is located at **Yojana Bhawan**, **Sansad Marg**, **New Delhi**.
 
• **Policy Functions:** The organization performs **Strategic and Long-term Policy** and program frameworks, and monitors their progress through **data-driven governance**.
</ul

questions.question: The Himalayan High Altitude Atmospheric and Climate Research Centre was inaugurated on 8th April 2025 in which district?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Udhampur**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Himalayan High Altitude Atmospheric and Climate Research Centre was inaugurated on **8th April 2025** in the Udhampur district of Jammu and Kashmir.
 
• The centre aims to **study atmospheric and climatic changes** in the Himalayan region, which is highly sensitive to global climate change.
 
• It will serve as a key research hub for monitoring **weather patterns, air quality, and greenhouse gas emissions** in high-altitude environments.
 
• The facility is equipped with advanced instruments to **track and analyze microclimatic changes** and their impact on biodiversity, water resources, and glacial health.
 
• This initiative is part of India’s efforts to enhance scientific research on climate resilience and its impact on **socio-economic and ecological systems**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Climate Change in the Himalayas**

 
 
• The Himalayan region is often referred to as the "Third Pole" due to its vast glacial cover, which is a vital source of freshwater for millions of people.
 
• Rising temperatures and erratic weather patterns have accelerated the **melting of glaciers**, leading to increased risks of glacial lake outburst floods (GLOFs).
 
• Studies indicate that the Himalayas are warming at a faster rate than the global average, making it a crucial area for climate research.
 
 
 
• **High-Altitude Atmospheric Research**
 
 
• High-altitude research involves studying atmospheric components such as aerosols, clouds, and greenhouse gases, which significantly impact weather and climate systems.
 
• Such studies help in understanding the **role of aerosols** in cloud formation and precipitation patterns.
 
 
 
• **Impact on Biodiversity**
 
 
• The Himalayas host a rich array of flora and fauna, many of which are endemic to the region.
 
• Climate change poses a threat to this biodiversity, leading to shifts in species distribution and habitat loss.
 
 
 
• **India’s Climate Research Initiatives**
 
 
• India has established several high-altitude research stations, including the Himadri station in the Arctic, to study global climate interactions.
 
• These initiatives align with India’s commitment to the **Paris Agreement** on climate change and sustainable development goals.

questions.question: Which organisation planned a big safety drill called 'Operation Abhyaas' in May 2025 to help people prepare for emergencies?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**National Disaster Management Authority (NDMA)**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Operation Abhyaas** is a comprehensive safety and disaster preparedness drill scheduled to be conducted in **May 2025**.
 
• The initiative is spearheaded by the **National Disaster Management Authority (NDMA)**, which serves as the apex body for disaster management in **India**.
 
• The primary objective of this exercise is to enhance the response capabilities of various agencies, including the **National Disaster Response Force (NDRF)**, and to test the effectiveness of existing **emergency protocols**.
 
• The drill focuses on creating realistic **simulations** of natural and man-made disasters, such as **earthquakes**, **floods**, and **industrial accidents**, to ensure that the **State Disaster Management Authorities (SDMAs)** and **District Disaster Management Authorities (DDMAs)** are fully prepared for any exigency.
 
• The exercise is designed to identify gaps in **communication**, **resource allocation**, and **evacuation strategies** before actual emergencies occur. ***Hence, the option identifying NDMA as the planning organization is correct.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **National Disaster Management Authority (NDMA):**

 
 
• The **NDMA** was formally constituted on **27th September 2006**, under the **Disaster Management Act, 2005**.
 
• It is chaired by the **Prime Minister of India** and has a vice-chairman and nine other members.
 
• Its primary mandate is to lay down policies, plans, and guidelines for disaster management to ensure a **timely and effective response** to disasters.
 
 
 
• **National Disaster Response Force (NDRF):**
 
 
• The **NDRF** is a specialized force constituted "for the purpose of specialist response to a threatening disaster situation or disaster" under the **Act of 2005**.
 
• It currently consists of **16 battalions** organized on paramilitary lines and equipped to handle **CBRN (Chemical, Biological, Radiological, and Nuclear)** emergencies as well.
 
 
 
• **Other Organizations Mentioned:**
 
 
• **Defence Research and Development Organisation (DRDO):** Established in **1958**, it focuses on developing **defense technologies** and hardware for the **Indian Armed Forces**.
 
• **Department of Military Affairs (DMA):** Created in **December 2019**, it is headed by the **Chief of Defence Staff (CDS)** and deals with the integration of the three services.
 
• **Defence Equipment Exporters Association (DEEA):** Primarily focuses on the **promotion** and **export** of Indian-made military hardware to other **countries**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Institutional Framework:** The **Disaster Management Act, 2005**, envisages a three-tier structure consisting of the **NDMA** at the national level, **SDMAs** at the state level, and **DDMAs** at the district level.
 
• **Vulnerability Profile:** Approximately **58.6%** of the Indian landmass is prone to **earthquakes** of moderate to very high intensity, making drills like **Operation Abhyaas** critical for **public safety**.
 
• **International Collaboration:** NDMA aligns its strategies with the **Sendai Framework for Disaster Risk Reduction (2015–2030)**, which aims for a substantial reduction of disaster risk and losses in lives, livelihoods, and health.
 
• **Early Warning Systems:** NDMA works closely with the **India Meteorological Department (IMD)** and the **Indian National Centre for Ocean Information Services (INCOIS)** to disseminate **real-time alerts** to the **population**.

• **Nizamabad Region:**
 
 
• **Nizamabad** is often referred to as the “**Turmeric City**” due to its extensive turmeric production.
 
• The region has a climate and soil type that are conducive to turmeric cultivation.
 
• The **Nizamabad Agricultural Market** is one of the largest turmeric markets in Asia.
 
 
 
• **National Turmeric Board:**
 
 
• The **National Turmeric Board** was established to address the challenges faced by turmeric farmers, such as market fluctuations and lack of proper infrastructure.
 
• It aims to create a centralized system for managing turmeric production, quality control, and export logistics.
 
• It will also facilitate **scientific research** to improve the yield and quality of turmeric crops.
 
 
 
• **Turmeric's Importance:**
 
 
• Turmeric has significant **medicinal properties**, including anti-inflammatory and antioxidant effects.
 
• It is a key ingredient in traditional Indian medicine systems like **Ayurveda** and **Siddha**.
 
• The global demand for turmeric has increased due to its use in health supplements and natural remedies.
